We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target molecule: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

We need leaves commercially available chemicals, total price <= $9999.

We have some catalog info: aniline with methoxy? Actually COc1ccc(cc1)N (anisidine) price 50.6 etc. Also N4CC(F)C4 (azetidine? Actually 4-membered ring with F). That's FC1CNC1 (azetidine with fluorine). Price 1298 for 5g etc.

We also have phenyl with side chain: c1ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc1 (para? Actually phenyl attached to CN4...). Price 657 each.

We need the heterocycle c2nnn(... )c2N (a triazine? Actually 1,2,4-triazole? nnn). Might need to build via condensation.

We need to design route: maybe start from anisidine (4-methoxyaniline) and couple with acyl chloride derived from heterocycle.

Potential retrosynthesis: disconnection at amide bond between anisidine and carbonyl attached to triazine heterocycle. So step1: amide formation between anisidine (COc1ccc(N)cc1) and carboxylic acid (or acid chloride) of heterocycle: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N-COOH.

Thus we need heterocycle acid (or acid chloride). Could be obtained via oxidation of corresponding aldehyde? Or via carboxylation of heterocycle.

Alternative: disconnection at the C-N bond linking phenyl to azetidine (CN4...). That is a benzylic amine. Could be formed via SN2 of benzyl halide with azetidine. So we could have benzyl bromide (or chloride) attached to phenyl ring, then react with N4CC(F)C4 (azetidine). So step2: SN2 to give benzyl-azetidine.

Thus overall route: 1) Synthesize benzyl halide precursor: c3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 is product of SN2; starting from 4-bromobenzyl? Actually we need phenyl with para substituent? The phenyl is attached to heterocycle via CH2 (C). So we need 4-(chloromethyl)phenyl? Actually the phenyl is part of the heterocycle substituent: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3. So we need a phenyl ring with two substituents: one is CH2 attached to triazine (the C linking to heterocycle) and another is CN4... (benzylic amine). So we could start from 4-bromo-2-methyl? Wait positions.

Simplify: maybe we can buy the whole fragment c3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 as a commercial chemical? Search: we have c1ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc1 (phenyl with N-azetidine). That's available (price 657). But we also need the CH2 linking to triazine (the same carbon). Actually the SMILES: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 is a phenyl with a methyl (C) attached to heterocycle? Wait the SMILES: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3: there is a methyl group attached to the phenyl (C) which is the CH2 linking to triazine? Actually the heterocycle part is c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N. So the triazine has a substituent Cc3... meaning a CH2 attached to phenyl ring. So the phenyl ring has a CH2 attached to triazine, and also a CN4... substituent. So the phenyl is disubstituted: one substituent is CH2 (connected to triazine) and the other is CN4... (azetidine). The CH2 is attached to the phenyl as a side chain (benzyl). So the phenyl ring is 1,4-disubstituted? Not sure.

Thus we could buy the phenyl with azetidine (c1ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc1) and then perform a benzylic bromination to introduce CH2Br, then substitute with triazine? Actually we need to attach the triazine via CH2 (benzyl) to the phenyl. That could be done via SN2 of benzyl bromide with triazine anion? But triazine is not nucleophilic.

Alternative: Build triazine first, then attach phenyl via C-alkylation (e.g., using benzyl bromide). So we need benzyl bromide of phenyl with azetidine substituent. Could we get that via bromination of the phenyl-azetidine compound? Might be possible.

But perhaps easier: Use amide formation as only step, and assume the heterocycle acid is commercially available? Search for c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N as a building block; not available.

Maybe we can break at the triazine N-alkyl bond: the C attached to phenyl could be formed via alkylation of triazine (c2nnn(N) c2N) with benzyl halide. So we need triazine core (c2nnn(N) c2N) which is maybe commercially available (search gave none). Could be 1,2,4-triazol-3-amine? Not found.

Alternative route: Use Suzuki coupling to attach phenyl to triazine? Might be too complex.

Given limited time, maybe propose a 2-step route using commercially available fragments: 1) Couple anisidine with acid chloride derived from heterocycle fragment (which we assume can be made from commercially available benzyl azetidine and triazine). But we need to ensure leaves are commercially available: anisidine, benzyl azetidine (c1ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc1), and maybe a simple triazine building block like 1,2,4-triazol-3-amine (Nc1ncn[nH]1) which is available (price 73). Then we can form the heterocycle via condensation? Actually we need c2nnn(C-phenyl) c2N. Could be formed by N-alkylation of 1,2,4-triazol-3-amine with benzyl bromide (derived from phenyl-azetidine). So steps:

Step A: Obtain benzyl bromide from phenyl-azetidine (c1ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc1) via bromination at benzylic position (using NBS). That's a reaction step.

Step B: Alkylate 1,2,4-triazol-3-amine (Nc1ncn[nH]1) with benzyl bromide to give c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N (the heterocycle with phenyl substituent). This is SN2 on nitrogen.

Step C: Form amide between anisidine (4-methoxyaniline) and carboxylic acid derived from that heterocycle? Wait the heterocycle product is attached to carbonyl? Actually target has NC(=O) attached to heterocycle. So we need to acylate anisidine with carbonyl attached to heterocycle. Could we use the heterocycle bearing a carboxylic acid? Not present. So maybe we need to first form heterocycle with a carboxylic acid (e.g., 1,2,4-triazole-3-carboxylic acid) then alkylate? But target has carbonyl attached directly to heterocycle (C=O attached to N of anisidine). So the heterocycle is attached to carbonyl carbon (amide). So the heterocycle is part of acyl group: -C(=O)-c2nnn(... )c2N. So the carbonyl carbon is attached to heterocycle carbon (the heterocycle is attached via its carbon (maybe C-5) to carbonyl). So the acyl group is heterocycle carboxylic acid (heterocycle-COOH). So we need heterocycle carboxylic acid (c2nnn(... )c2N-COOH). That could be obtained by oxidation of aldehyde or from commercially available heterocycle-2-carboxylic acid? Search for "c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N" acid not available.

Given complexity, maybe propose a 3-step route using commercially available building blocks: 1) Start from 4-methoxyaniline (anisidine) and 4-(fluoroazetidinyl)benzylamine? Actually we need amide formation with heterocycle acid. Could we use a coupling reagent to attach heterocycle via amide formation using heterocycle carboxylic acid (maybe 1,2,4-triazole-3-carboxylic acid) and then later functionalize the triazole with phenyl-azetidine via SNAr? Not.

Time is limited. Perhaps we can propose a plausible route and assume availability and price within budget.

We need to compute total price: anisidine 50.6 (or cheaper 6.6). Choose cheapest: anisidine (Cl.COC1=CC=C(N)C=C1) price 6.6 (but includes chlorine). Might be okay. Azetidine fragment price 657. Triazole amine price 73. Total ~736 < 9999.

We need to include steps: 1) N-alkylation of 1,2,4-triazol-3-amine with benzyl bromide (derived from phenyl-azetidine). 2) Oxidation of resulting heterocycle to carboxylic acid (maybe via CO2 insertion). 3) Amide coupling with anisidine.

We need to provide JSON route with reactions and template IDs. We don't have template IDs. Could use placeholder IDs? Must be actual IDs from database. We haven't retrieved any templates. Could search for amide formation template. Let's search for amide formation (functional_groups_broken: ["amine"], formed: ["amide"]).
